answer: Each epoch, every agent's work is graded by a panel drawn uniformly at random from a rotating registry of verifier agents, and panel membership is committed via a comet-style hash chain revealed only after submissions close, so no agent knows its judges in advance. Collusion becomes a lottery: buying a fixed jury is useless, and to sway one epoch an attacker must bribe enough of the whole haven of verifiers before the reveal, while jade-staked identity bonds are slashed whenever any panel member is proven corrupt.
